definition_zh: 利润；盈利；收益；益处
definition_en: the money gained after costs are paid, or any advantage gained from an action
core_image: 集市收摊后，两张桌子并排：一张放本钱，一张放收回的钱，后者多出一小堆
scene: 集市收摊后，摊主把本钱与收回的钱分放两处，收回的那边多出一小堆。After a strong season, the bakery finally turned a profit.
sceneCN: 摊主把本钱和货款分开放，货款那边多出一小堆；句中的 profit 指「扣除成本后剩下的钱」（第 1 个义项：经营所得减去成本后的净增益）。图中可辨识物件：两张木桌、钱箱、账本、面包篮、收摊的布；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 利润；盈利；收益；益处
得益；获利

senses.title: Money left after costs
senses.definition: the money that remains from income after all costs of producing or selling have been paid
senses.definitionCN: 收入在支付全部生产或销售成本后剩下的钱
senses.example: After a strong season, the bakery finally turned a profit.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个旺季，这家面包店终于开始盈利。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'to make progress', and profit is the advance a business makes beyond what it spent.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「向前推进」，而利润就是企业在收回花费之后向前多走的那一步。

senses.title: Gain from a single sale
senses.definition: the gain made when something is sold for more than it cost
senses.definitionCN: 把某物以高于成本的价格卖出时得到的增益
senses.example: They sold the old press at a profit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把旧印刷机卖掉，赚了一笔。
senses.why: A single transaction repeats the whole logic in miniature: buy low, sell higher, keep the difference.
senses.whyCN: 单笔交易把整套逻辑缩小重演：低价买入、高价卖出、留下差额。

senses.title: The motive to seek gain
senses.definition: the incentive to act because of the gain expected, especially in economic life
senses.definitionCN: 因预期收益而行动的驱动力，尤见于经济生活
senses.example: The profit motive drove the expansion into new markets.
senses.exampleCN: 营利动机推动企业向新市场扩张。
senses.why: Once profit is a regular result, it becomes a reason for acting, and the word names the reason.
senses.whyCN: 一旦利润成为常规结果，它就成了行动的理由，而这个词也就用来指这个理由。

senses.title: Gross profit before deductions
senses.definition: sales revenue minus the direct cost of goods, before other expenses are subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 销售收入减去商品的直接成本，尚未扣除其他费用
senses.example: Gross profit looked healthy, but rent ate most of it.
senses.exampleCN: 毛利看起来不错，但房租吃掉了大半。
senses.why: Accounts separate direct costs from overheads, so profit is split into layers and the first layer gets a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 会计把直接成本与间接费用分开，于是利润被分层，第一层配上一个限定词。

senses.title: Net profit after all charges
senses.titleCN: 扣除全部费用后的净利润
senses.definition: the final profit after every cost, tax and charge has been subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 扣除所有成本、税款与费用之后的最终利润
senses.example: Net profit for the year was smaller than the headline figure suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 全年净利润比标题数字所显示的要少。
senses.why: The last layer is what owners actually keep, so it is marked off from the earlier, flattering layers.
senses.whyCN: 最后一层才是所有者真正留下的，因此要与前面那些更好看的层次区分开。

senses.title: Profit as a ratio of sales
senses.titleCN: 以销售额为基准的利润率
senses.definition: profit expressed as a percentage of revenue, showing how much of each sale is kept
senses.definitionCN: 以收入百分比表示的利润，显示每笔销售能留下多少
senses.example: A thin profit margin leaves little room for a price cut.
senses.exampleCN: 利润率很薄，几乎没有降价空间。
senses.why: Absolute profit cannot compare firms of different size, so it is turned into a margin, a share of each sale.
senses.whyCN: 绝对利润无法比较规模不同的企业，于是把它转成利润率，即每笔销售中的占比。

senses.title: Advantage in a broad sense
senses.definition: a benefit or advantage gained from an activity, not necessarily financial
senses.definitionCN: 从某项活动中获得的益处，未必与金钱有关
senses.example: He read the old manuals to his profit.
senses.exampleCN: 他读那些旧手册，从中获益。
senses.why: Before profit was narrowed to money, it meant any forward gain, and that older sense survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 在利润被收窄为金钱之前，它泛指任何前进式的获益，这一旧义仍存于正式书面语中。

senses.title: Any gain from an action
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何行动带来的净增益
senses.definition: whatever is gained from an action once its costs, including effort and risk, are counted
senses.definitionCN: 把努力与风险等代价计入后，行动所带来的任何净增益
senses.example: The expedition showed a profit in knowledge if not in money.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考察若不以金钱计，则在知识上有收益。
senses.why: Generalised, profit is simply the surplus of return over outlay, whatever the currency of each side.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，利润就是回报超出投入的剩余，无论两边用的是什么「货币」。

intro.en: Profit came through Old French from Latin profectus 'progress, advance', the past participle of proficere 'to accomplish', built on pro- 'forward' and facere 'to do, make'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: profit 经古法语来自拉丁语 profectus「进展、前进」，它是 proficere「完成、取得进展」的过去分词，由表「向前」的前缀与 facere「做、造」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Facere meant 'to do, make'. Its deeper root is reconstructed, and it is the source of a very large family including effect, factory and difficult.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」。其更早词根属重构形式，它是包括 effect、factory、difficult 在内一大族词的来源。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere produced proficere, 'to make progress, to accomplish, to be useful'.
items.cn: 表「向前」的前缀加 facere 构成 proficere，意为「取得进展、完成、有用」。

items.en: Its past participle profectus was used as a noun for 'progress, advance, gain', the sense that passed into French.
items.cn: 其过去分词 profectus 被用作名词，指「进展、前进、增益」，这一意义传入了法语。

items.en: Old French prufit or profit meant 'advantage, gain', and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century first as a general benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 prufit 或 profit 意为「好处、增益」，英语在十四世纪借入，最初泛指益处。

items.en: The financial surplus sense hardened in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and gross, net and margin later divided it into layers.
items.cn: 财务盈余义在十六、十七世纪逐渐固定；后来毛利、净利与利润率又把它分成几层。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date of the financial sense is not settled, and the pre-Latin root of facere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：财务义的确切出现年代没有定论，facere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes and sound-alikes, including one that is not related at all; group two holds words for money gained, each measured at a different point.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词，其中有一个根本不同源；第二组都指获得的钱，但计量的位置不同。

entries.definition: A person who foretells the future, from Greek prophētēs 'one who speaks for a god'; it sounds identical to profit but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 指预言未来的人，来自希腊语 prophētēs「代神发言者」；与 profit 同音，却完全不同源。

entries.definition: Describes something that yields profit; it cannot replace the noun that names the gain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能带来利润的事物；不能取代指利润本身的名词。

entries.definition: Someone who makes excessive profit, especially in a shortage; the ending adds a tone of blame.
entries.definitionCN: 指牟取过厚利润的人，尤见于短缺时期；词尾带有谴责语气。

entries.definition: Yielding no gain; it negates the adjective rather than naming a loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有收益的；它否定的是形容词，而不是指亏损。

entries.definition: An increase in money or advantage; broader and less technical than profit.
entries.definitionCN: 金钱或好处的增加；比 profit 更宽泛，也不那么技术化。

entries.definition: The profit a company reports to its owners, often used interchangeably with profit in finance.
entries.definitionCN: 公司向所有者报告的利润，在金融语境中常与 profit 互用。

entries.definition: Money received from sales before any cost is deducted; profit is what survives the deduction.
entries.definitionCN: 销售中收到的钱，尚未扣除任何成本；profit 是扣除后幸存的部分。

entries.definition: The gain on an investment expressed as a proportion of what was put in.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收益按投入比例表示的增益。

entries.definition: The amount by which income exceeds outgoings, often used of public accounts rather than private firms.
entries.definitionCN: 收入超出支出的部分，常用于公共账目而非私人企业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin steps, the real family and the real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语演变、真实词族与真实会计搭配。

normal.en: The root means 'to make forward': profit is the step a business takes beyond its costs.
normal.cn: 词根意为「向前做成」：利润就是企业越过成本向前多走的一步。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, profitably, profiteer.
normal.cn: 词族包括 profit、profitable、profitability、profitably、profiteer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the accounts: gross profit, net profit, profit margin.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出账目层次：毛利、净利、利润率。

normal.en: The same root appears in factory and effect, both built on the verb 'to make'.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 factory 与 effect 中，二者都建立在「做」这个动词上。

normal.en: Profit is what is left; revenue is what came in.
normal.cn: 利润是留下来的；收入是进来的。

abstract.en: Picture two piles on a table, one for what was spent and one for what came back.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两堆钱，一堆是花出去的，一堆是收回来的。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose lowest rung is cost and whose top rung is what the owner keeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最下面一级是成本，最上面一级是所有者留下的。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall that packs up only after the till is heavier than the stock was.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位，只有钱箱比原先的货更沉时才收摊。

examples.en: The cooperative distributes its profit among the members.
examples.cn: 合作社把利润分配给成员。

examples.en: Rising costs squeezed the profit margin to almost nothing.
examples.cn: 成本上升把利润率压到几乎为零。

examples.en: She studied the old maps to her profit.
examples.cn: 她研读旧地图，从中获益。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不（pro）费（fit）」——成本没有白费，多出来的那部分就是利润

root: 拉丁语 profectus（进展、增益），来自 proficere（取得进展）＝pro-（向前）＋facere（做、造）；经古法语 profit 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one surplus: something comes back larger than it went out, and the word then names a single sale's gain, the motive behind it, the layered accounts of gross and net, the margin, an older sense of general benefit, and finally any surplus of return over outlay.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份剩余展开：回流之物比付出之物更大；这个词再指单笔交易的赚头、背后的动机、毛利与净利的分层账目、利润率、较早的泛指益处，最后指任何回报超出投入的剩余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two piles of money on a table, and the returning pile is the taller one.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上两堆钱，收回来那堆更高。

branches.en: SURPLUS: the whole business and a single sale both end with more than they began with.
branches.cn: 剩余：整个生意与单笔交易都以「比开始时多」收尾。

branches.en: MOTIVE: expected gain becomes the reason to act, and the word shifts from result to cause.
branches.cn: 动机：预期收益成为行动的理由，这个词便从结果转指原因。

branches.en: LAYERS: direct costs and overheads cut the surplus into gross and net.
branches.cn: 分层：直接成本与间接费用把剩余切成毛利与净利。

branches.en: RATIO: dividing profit by sales makes it comparable across firms.
branches.cn: 比率：把利润除以销售额，使它能在企业之间比较。

branches.en: OLD AND GENERAL: the earliest sense of any forward benefit survives in formal prose and then widens to every kind of return.
branches.cn: 旧义与泛义：最早的「任何前进式益处」存于正式书面语，继而扩展到各种回报。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb 'to make', and the family around it keeps that same shape.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀加一个意为「做」的拉丁动词构成，周围的词族也保持同样的结构。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- and facere build proficere and its participle profectus, which French shortened into the noun English took over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的前缀与 facere 构成 proficere 及其分词 profectus，法语将其缩短为英语接手的名词。

items.example: The prefix gives the sense of moving ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀赋予「向前走」的意思。

items.example: The root is one of the busiest in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是英语中最活跃的词根之一。

items.example: The verb names moving forward by doing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指靠「做」向前推进。

items.example: The participle became a noun of advance.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了表示前进的名词。

items.example: The year ended with a small profit.
items.exampleCN: 这一年以小额利润收尾。
这种作物证明是有利可图的。
这片土地被以获利的方式耕作。

items.example: Profiteers raised prices during the shortage.
items.exampleCN: 短缺期间，牟利者抬高了价格。

definition_zh: 计划；节目；计算机程序；为……编写程序
definition_en: a written plan of action, a list or show, or a set of coded instructions; to arrange or write such instructions
core_image: 墙上贴着一张写满时间与步骤的纸，旁边的旧机器照着纸条上的指令一行行运行
scene: 工作室的墙上贴着一张写满时间与步骤的纸，旁边的旧机器正照着纸条上的指令一行行运行。The engineer loaded the program and watched the machine follow each line.
sceneCN: 这里 program 指交给计算机执行的一整套指令（第 4 个义项：计算机程序）；句意：工程师载入程序，看着机器逐行执行。图中可辨识物件：墙上的时间表、纸条、旧机器、指示灯；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 计划；节目；程序
编排；为……编写程序

derivatives.zh: 纲领性的；按计划行事的

senses.title: A plan of future action
senses.definition: a set of intended actions arranged in advance to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个目标而事先安排好的一系列行动
senses.example: The city launched a housing program for low-income families.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府启动了一项面向低收入家庭的住房计划。
senses.why: the Greek noun began as a public notice written down ahead of time, so the word still carries the idea of something laid out before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词最初指事先写好的公开通告，因此这个词始终带着「事情发生之前就摆好的安排」这一层意思。

senses.title: An order of events
senses.definition: a list showing the times and order of the parts of an event
senses.definitionCN: 列出活动各部分时间与顺序的清单
senses.example: The conference program lists every talk and the room it uses.
senses.exampleCN: 会议日程列出了每场报告及其所在房间。
senses.why: a written notice of what will happen and when is the most literal survival of the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 把「将发生什么、何时发生」写下来通告，正是原义最直接的延续。

senses.title: A printed list for an audience
senses.definition: the printed sheet given to an audience, naming the performers and the works
senses.definitionCN: 发给观众、写明演出者与曲目的印刷纸页
senses.example: She read the program before the orchestra tuned up.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团调音之前，她先读了节目单。
senses.why: theatres turned the order of a performance into a small printed booklet, and the booklet took the name of the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 剧院把演出顺序做成一本小册子，册子便直接沿用了「顺序」这个名字。

senses.title: A show that is broadcast
senses.definition: a single show or an ongoing series carried by a station
senses.definitionCN: 由电台或电视台播出的单个节目或系列节目
senses.example: The station dropped the program after one season.
senses.exampleCN: 电视台播出一季后停掉了这个节目。
senses.why: broadcasting inherited the word from theatre: each slot in the schedule is a program, whether or not paper is involved.
senses.whyCN: 广播沿用了剧院的说法：节目表上的每一个时段都叫一个节目，与纸张已无关系。

senses.title: Instructions a computer follows
senses.definition: an ordered set of coded instructions that makes a computer carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 使计算机完成一项任务的有序编码指令集合
senses.example: The program sorts the files by date and deletes the copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序按日期排序文件并删除重复副本。
senses.why: the earliest electronic machines were fed a written sequence of steps, exactly like a plan handed to a reader, so the plan word moved onto the machine.
senses.whyCN: 最早的电子机器接收的是一份写好的步骤序列，就像交给读者的一份计划，于是「计划」这个词就移到了机器上。

senses.title: A course of study
senses.definition: an organized course or set of courses leading to a qualification
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种资格的有组织课程或课程组合
senses.example: The new program leads to a master's degree in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新课程两年后可获硕士学位。
senses.why: schools borrowed the plan word because a degree is also a sequence of steps that a student is expected to complete in order.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了「计划」这个词，因为拿学位同样是一串要求学生按顺序完成的步骤。

senses.title: A government or agency scheme
senses.definition: an official scheme that organizes money and staff for a public purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为公共目的组织资金与人员的官方方案
senses.example: The literacy program trained teachers in three rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫盲计划在三个农村县培训了教师。
senses.why: public bodies write down what they intend to do and fund it, and that funded intention is called a program.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构把打算做的事写下来并拨款，这份带钱的打算就被称为项目。

senses.title: To set something to happen
senses.definition: to arrange for a device or system to act at a set time or in a set way
senses.definitionCN: 安排某个设备或系统在固定时间或以固定方式动作
senses.example: They programmed the lights to switch off at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把灯设定在午夜自动关闭。
senses.why: once a machine can hold its own sequence of steps, the verb means putting that sequence into it, even when no code is written by hand.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机器能自己保存步骤序列，动词就表示把序列装进去，哪怕并没有手写代码。

senses.title: To write instructions for a machine
senses.definition: to write the code that a computer or machine will execute
senses.definitionCN: 编写计算机或机器将要执行的代码
senses.example: He programmed the robot to pick only the ripe fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他给机器人编程，让它只摘成熟的果子。
senses.why: this is the modern verb built directly on the computing noun: the programmer writes the plan the machine will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由计算机义名词转来的现代动词：程序员写下机器将要遵循的计划。

intro.en: Program is Greek in origin, Latin in transmission and French in form. Its oldest sense is a public notice written in advance; the computing sense is a twentieth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: program 源于希腊语，经拉丁语传递，形式取自法语。它最古老的意思是事先写好的公开通告；计算机义是二十世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek programma meant a public written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write. The noun named a posted announcement, not a scheme of action.
items.cn: 希腊语 programma 指公开的书面通告，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。这个名词指的是张贴出来的公告，而不是行动计划。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma as a learned noun for a written notice or preface, keeping the Greek shape and the written, public flavour.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 programma 作为书面通告或序言的学术名词，保留了希腊语的形式与「书面、公开」的色彩。

items.en: French programme entered English in the seventeenth century. English first used it for a public notice and soon for the printed order of a ceremony or performance.
items.cn: 法语 programme 在十七世纪进入英语。英语先用它指公开通告，很快又用它指仪式或演出的印刷顺序。

items.en: American printers shortened the ending to program. The two spellings now divide mainly by region, and the short form became standard in computing.
items.cn: 美国印刷者把词尾缩短为 program。两种拼写如今基本按地区分工，而短形式在计算机领域成为标准。

items.en: From the 1940s a program meant the coded sequence that drives a machine. The noun, and then the verb to program, followed the hardware into ordinary use.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，program 指驱动机器的编码序列。名词以及后来的动词「编程」随硬件一起进入日常使用。

items.en: The chain from Greek programma through Latin programma and French programme to English program is documented. Only the first written dates in English are approximate, and any Indo-European root proposed for graphein is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从希腊语 programma 经拉丁语 programma、法语 programme 到英语的这条链有文献依据，只是英语最早书证的年代为约数；为 graphein 提出的印欧语词根属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

note.en: The first group is the same word in other shapes and roles; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a plan, a timetable and software.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的其他形式与角色；第二组是与计划、时间表和软件相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, and the usual form for a printed list of performances; computing writing prefers program everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，也是节目单的常用形式；计算机写作各地多用 program。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code, not the code of one task; the noun names the work, while program names the product.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码这项活动，而不是某一任务的代码；名词指工作，program 指成品。

entries.definition: The person who writes the code; it answers who, where program answers what.
entries.definitionCN: 指写代码的人；它回答「谁」，而 program 回答「什么」。

entries.definition: Built on the Greek noun with a Latinised ending: it describes something done by fixed plan, as in programmatic music or programmatic reform.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊名词加拉丁化词尾构成：描述按固定计划进行的事物，如标题音乐或按纲领推行的改革。

entries.definition: The broad intention and the steps meant to reach it; a program is usually a plan that has been written down, funded or scheduled.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体意图及实现它的步骤；program 通常是已写下来、已拨款或已排期的计划。

entries.definition: The arrangement of times and dates; a program may contain a schedule, but a schedule says only when, not what for.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间与日期的安排；program 里可能含 schedule，但时间表只说「何时」，不说「为何」。

entries.definition: Programs and data treated as a product or a body of material; one program is a single unit of software.
entries.definitionCN: 把程序与数据当作产品与整套材料；一个 program 是软件的一个单元。

entries.definition: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting; it is a program for a discussion rather than for a machine or a season.
entries.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单；它是讨论的程序，而非机器或演出季的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek pro- means before and graphein means write, so a program is something written down before it happens.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pro- 意为「在前」，graphein 意为「书写」，所以 program 就是事先写下来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs program, programme, programming, programmer, programmable and programmatic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programme、programming、programmer、programmable 与 programmatic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the plan sense: training program, welfare program, housing program.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示「计划」义：培训计划、福利计划、住房计划。

normal.en: The two spellings differ only in the ending, and computing settles on program everywhere.
normal.cn: 两种拼写只差词尾，计算机领域各地都落在 program 上。

normal.en: The verb splits by object: you program a computer with code, and you program a timer with a setting.
normal.cn: 动词按宾语分工：给计算机编程是写代码，给定时器设程序是调设定。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill that keeps fluttering after the audience has gone, still deciding the order of a night that is over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张观众散场后仍在飘动的节目单，还在决定一个已经结束的夜晚的顺序。

abstract.en: Picture a strip of paper sliding into a machine, and the machine growing a spine as it reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条滑进机器，机器一边读一边长出脊骨。

abstract.en: Picture traffic lights blinking to a timetable nobody in the street can see.
abstract.cn: 想象街上的红绿灯按一张路人看不见的时间表眨眼。

examples.en: A well-written program can be read by another person without running it.
examples.cn: 写得好的程序，别人不运行也能读懂。

examples.en: The museum program lists four lectures and one concert.
examples.cn: 博物馆的活动日程列出四场讲座和一场音乐会。

examples.en: She programmed the irrigation system to water the field before dawn.
examples.cn: 她把灌溉系统设定在黎明前浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来个（gram）」——事先扑上去写下来的东西，就是计划与程序

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；计算机义始于二十世纪四十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one thread: something is written down in advance, first as a notice, then as an order of events, a printed list, a show, a set of machine instructions, a course, a funded scheme, and at last as the act of setting or coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条线索展开：某事被事先写下来，先是通告，再是活动顺序、印刷节目单、播出节目、机器指令集、课程、拨款项目，最后是设定与编程这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of times and steps pinned to the wall, with a machine reading the sheet line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满时间与步骤的纸钉在墙上，机器一行行读着这张纸。

branches.en: PLAN AND SCHEME: an intention set down in advance, whether a household plan or a funded public scheme.
branches.cn: 计划与方案：事先写下的意图，无论家务安排还是拨款推行的公共项目。

branches.en: TIME ARRANGEMENT: an order of events in time, applied to people and then to devices that must act on cue.
branches.cn: 时间安排：按时间排出的活动顺序，先用于人，后用于必须按时动作的设备。

branches.en: LIST AND SHOW: the printed order becomes a booklet, and the booklet gives its name to the broadcast item.
branches.cn: 节目单与节目：印刷的顺序成为小册子，小册子又把名字让给播出的节目。

branches.en: CODE: the written sequence is now for a machine, first as a noun and then as the verb that puts it there.
branches.cn: 代码：写下的序列改为给机器用，先是名词，再是把序列装进去的动词。

branches.en: COURSE OF STUDY: a degree is also a sequence of steps completed in order, so schools use the same word.
branches.cn: 课程：学位同样是一串按顺序完成的步骤，学校于是沿用同一个词。

intro.en: Program is Greek in its two pieces, Latin in its noun ending and French in its modern shape. English then added -ing, -er and -able to build the computing family.
intro.cn: program 的两个构件来自希腊语，名词词尾来自拉丁语，现代形式来自法语。英语随后加 -ing、-er、-able 构成计算机词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin programma is the one learned borrowing that carries the word from Greek into French and English; the other Latin-looking ending -atic came later through French adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 programma 是把这个词从希腊语带到法语与英语的唯一学术借词；另一个似拉丁的词尾 -atic 是后来经法语形容词进入的。

items.example: The prefix places the writing ahead of the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「写」放在事情发生之前。

items.example: The verb names the act of setting marks down.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把符号落下来的动作。

items.example: The ending turns the act of writing into a written thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「写」这个动作变成「写出来的东西」。

items.example: The Greek noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: a notice; an order of events
items.example: English took the French shape in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪接受了法语的形式。

items.meaning: a plan or a coded instruction set
items.example: The short spelling became standard in computing.
items.exampleCN: 短拼写在计算机领域成为标准。

items.example: Programming names the work rather than the product.
items.exampleCN: programming 指这项工作，而不是成品。

items.example: A programmer is the one who writes the code.
A programmable device can hold a new sequence.
items.exampleCN: 可编程设备能装入新的序列。

items.example: Programmatic music follows a written story.
items.exampleCN: 标题音乐遵循一个写好的故事。

definition_zh: 节目；节目单；计划；方案；（计算机）程序；规划；用程序控制
definition_en: a show or broadcast, a plan of events, a set of instructions for a computer, or the act of arranging such things
core_image: 一页预先写好的清单，把要演出的曲目和要做的事按顺序排在上面
scene: 演出开始前，音乐厅门口的桌上放着一叠薄薄的小册子，观众一边排队一边翻看今晚的曲目。The orchestra printed a slim programme listing every piece for the evening.
sceneCN: 这里取「节目单、节目」的意思（第 1 个义项：广播或演出的节目及其说明）；句意为乐团印了一本薄薄的节目单，列出当晚的每一首曲子。门口那叠小册子就是线索。

pos.zh: 节目；节目单；计划；方案；（计算机）程序
规划；安排；用程序控制

derivatives.zh: 由 programme 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「程序员」
由 programme 去 e 加 -ing 构成，义为「编程；节目编排」
由希腊词干 programmat- 加 -ic 构成，义为「纲领性的；按计划行事的」

senses.title: A show on television or radio
senses.definition: a show broadcast on television or radio, or the printed list of items in a performance
senses.definitionCN: 在电视或广播中播出的节目，也指演出前印好的曲目或环节清单
senses.example: Her cookery programme is shown every Sunday evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她的烹饪节目每周日晚播出。
senses.why: Greek programma was a public written notice, so the word began as something written down and read out before it named what was performed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 programma 本指公开写出的通告，所以这个词最初是「写下来给人看的东西」，后来才指被演出或被播出的内容。

senses.title: A plan of events or actions
senses.definition: an organized plan listing the events, steps or work that will be done
senses.definitionCN: 把要做的事件、步骤或工作有条理地列出来的计划
senses.example: The government launched a programme to repair rural roads.
senses.exampleCN: 政府启动了修缮乡村道路的计划。
senses.why: A written notice also fixes an order, so the same word came to mean the ordered list of things to be done.
senses.whyCN: 写出来的通告同时规定了顺序，于是同一个词又指「按顺序排好的待办事项」，也就是计划。

senses.title: A set of instructions for a computer
senses.definition: a series of coded instructions that makes a computer perform a task
senses.definitionCN: 让计算机完成某项任务的一串编码指令
senses.example: He wrote a short programme that sorts the names alphabetically.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一个短程序，把姓名按字母顺序排序。
senses.why: A computer follows a written sequence step by step, exactly as a theatre follows a printed running order, so the plan sense was reused for machine instructions.
senses.whyCN: 计算机一步步照着写好的顺序执行，就像剧场照着印好的流程单演出，于是「计划」这层意思被挪去指机器指令。

senses.title: To plan or arrange something
senses.definition: to arrange or set out a plan for an event, a machine or a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 为某项活动、某台机器或某个行动方案做出安排
senses.example: The festival was programmed months in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日的活动提前几个月就安排好了。
senses.why: If a programme is a written order of events, then to programme is to put things into that order, and later to feed that order into a machine.
senses.whyCN: 既然 programme 是写好的事件顺序，那么动词就是「把事情排进这个顺序」，后来也指把顺序输入机器。

intro.en: Programme goes back through French to a Greek word for a public written notice, built from a prefix meaning before and a verb meaning to write.
intro.cn: programme 经法语上溯到一个希腊词，本指公开写出的通告，由表示「在前」的前缀和表示「写」的动词构成。

items.en: The Greek prefix pro- meant before or in front, and graphein meant to write, so the pair described writing something beforehand.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 pro- 表示「在前」，动词 graphein 表示「写」，两者合起来就是「事先写出」。

items.en: Programma named a public notice put up in advance, such as an official announcement or a posted list.
items.cn: programma 指提前张贴出来的公开通告，例如官方告示或贴出的名单。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma unchanged from Greek and kept the sense of a written public notice.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入 programma，仍指写出来的公开通告。

items.en: French programme narrowed the word towards the printed list of a performance and towards a plan of work.
items.cn: 法语 programme 把词义收窄到演出的印刷节目单，以及工作的计划。

items.en: English took the French form as programme, kept it in Britain, and American usage shortened it to program.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 programme，英式保留此拼写，美式则简化为 program。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and relatives built on the same Greek root for writing; the near-meaning group gathers words for shows and plans.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「写」词根上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示节目与计划的词。

entries.definition: The shorter American spelling, used for shows, plans and computer code.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的美式拼写，同样表示节目、计划与计算机代码。

entries.definition: A person who writes instructions for a computer.
entries.definitionCN: 编写计算机指令的人；程序员。

entries.definition: The work of writing computer code, or of arranging a schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 编写计算机代码的工作，或安排日程的工作。

entries.definition: Planned and organized according to a fixed set of aims.
entries.definitionCN: 按照一套固定目标来计划与组织的；纲领性的。

entries.definition: A performance or broadcast intended to entertain an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为娱乐观众而演出或播出的内容。

entries.definition: A radio or television transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 广播或电视的播出。

entries.definition: A plan that lists times and events.
entries.definitionCN: 列出时间与事项的计划；日程表。

entries.definition: A large plan, often official, for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而制定的大型计划，常指官方方案。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a written notice, so its memories hang on writing, listing and ordering, and on the machine that now follows such a list.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一份写出来的通告，所以记忆可以挂在「写、列、排序」上，也挂在照着清单执行的机器上。

normal.en: Greek graphein means to write, and English keeps that root in programme, diagram and grammar.
normal.cn: 希腊语 graphein 意为「写」，英语在 programme、diagram、grammar 里都保留了这个词根。

normal.en: The prefix pro- means before, so a programme is literally something written before the event happens.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示「在前」，所以 programme 字面上就是「活动开始之前写好的东西」。

normal.en: A theatre programme lists items in order and a computer program lists steps in order; the same idea of a written order runs through both.
normal.cn: 剧场节目单按顺序列出节目，计算机程序按顺序列出步骤，两者贯穿的是同一个「写好的顺序」。

normal.en: British English keeps the final -me and the double m, while American English drops them to spell it program.
normal.cn: 英式保留词尾的 me 与双写的 m，美式则省去这些字母，写成 program。

normal.en: Programmer only adds -er to the noun: the person who writes the code.
normal.cn: programmer 只是在名词后加 -er，指写代码的人。

abstract.en: A word that began as a poster and ended as code shows how writing can turn into action.
abstract.cn: 一个从海报变成代码的词，说明写下来的东西可以变成真正的行动。

abstract.en: Every list is a small promise about the future, which is why a show and a plan share one name.
abstract.cn: 每份清单都是对未来的小小承诺，所以一场演出和一份计划共用一个名字。

abstract.en: The machine does not invent the order; it only obeys the order that someone wrote down.
abstract.cn: 机器不会自己发明顺序，它只服从别人写下来的顺序。

examples.en: Her cookery programme is shown every Sunday evening.
examples.cn: 她的烹饪节目每周日晚播出。

examples.en: The city has programmed the traffic lights to favour buses.
examples.cn: 这座城市把交通灯设置成优先放行公交。

examples.en: Our school runs a programme for students who need extra help.
examples.cn: 我们学校为需要额外帮助的学生开办了一个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若格拉姆」——听着像「铺个栏目」，把栏目一条条铺开，就是节目单和计划。

root: 希腊语 pro-（在前）+ graphein（写）构成 programma，本指预先写出的公告；经拉丁语 programma 与法语 programme 进入英语，美式拼写简化为 program。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written list set out in advance; from it grow the show that follows the list, the plan behind it, the machine that executes it, and the act of arranging it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是事先写好的一份清单；由它长出照着清单演出的节目、清单背后的计划、执行清单的机器，以及安排清单的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pinned up before an event, listing what will happen and in what order.
core.cn: 核心意象：活动开始前贴出的一张纸，写着要发生什么、按什么顺序发生。

branches.en: a printed sheet folded inside a concert hall seat
branches.cn: 音乐厅座椅上折好的印刷节目单

branches.en: a notice board announcing next month's events
branches.cn: 公告板上预告下月活动的通知

branches.en: a minister signing a three-year building plan
branches.cn: 部长签署一份三年建设计划

branches.en: a screen waiting for a line of code to run
branches.cn: 屏幕上等待一行代码运行

branches.en: an engineer slotting steps into the right order
branches.cn: 工程师把各个步骤排进正确的顺序

intro.en: The word rests on a Greek prefix and a Greek verb of writing, then passes through Latin and French before English adds its own endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语前缀和表示「写」的动词支撑，经拉丁语与法语传入英语，再由英语加上自己的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin took programma straight from Greek and used it for a written notice; the same root produced gramma, a written mark or letter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 programma，指写出的通告；同一词根还产生 gramma，指写下的符号或字母。

items.meaning: a show, a plan, a set of code

definition_zh: 前进；行进；进步；进展；发展；使前进
definition_en: movement forward, especially towards a goal, or the gradual development and improvement of something
core_image: 一行人沿着山路一步步往上走，身后的路越拉越长
scene: 山路上的人已经走了大半程，回头还能看见来时的弯道。The hikers made slow progress up the ridge before the fog closed in.
sceneCN: 这里取「进展、前进的程度」的意思（第 2 个义项：朝更远或更好的状态发展）；句意为雾合拢之前，徒步者沿着山脊缓慢上行。回头可见的弯道说明他们已经走了很远。

pos.zh: 前进；进步；进展；发展
前进；行进；进步；发展

derivatives.zh: 由 progress 加 -ive 构成，义为「渐进的；进步的」
由 progress 加 -ion 构成，义为「进展；序列」
由 progressive 加 -ly 构成，义为「逐渐地」

senses.title: Forward movement towards a place
senses.definition: movement forward, especially of a group of people or a vehicle towards a destination
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，尤指人群或车辆朝目的地行进
senses.example: The army's progress through the valley was slowed by rain.
senses.exampleCN: 军队穿过山谷的行进被雨拖慢了。
senses.why: Latin progredi is built from pro-, forward, and gradi, to walk, so the first sense is simply walking forward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 progredi 由 pro-（向前）和 gradi（走）构成，所以最初的意思就是「往前走」。

senses.title: Development towards a better state
senses.definition: the gradual improvement or development of a person, a project or a society
senses.definitionCN: 个人、项目或社会逐渐变好或向前发展
senses.example: She has made real progress in her spoken English.
senses.exampleCN: 她的英语口语有了实实在在的进步。
senses.why: Walking forward easily turns into a metaphor for moving towards a goal, so the word came to mean any step towards something better.
senses.whyCN: 「往前走」很容易被用来比喻「朝目标迈进」，于是这个词就指任何向更好状态靠近的一步。

senses.title: To move forward
senses.definition: to move forward or continue on a course
senses.definitionCN: 向前移动，或沿某条路线继续前行
senses.example: The procession progressed slowly along the narrow street.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍沿着窄街缓慢前行。
senses.why: The verb keeps the literal Latin sense of walking on, and its stress falls on the second syllable, unlike the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「继续走」的本义，重音落在第二个音节上，与名词不同。

senses.title: To improve or develop
senses.definition: to develop or improve, especially over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里逐渐发展或变好
senses.example: Work on the new school is progressing faster than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校的工程进展比预期更快。
senses.why: Because the noun already meant improvement, the verb took on the same figurative sense and now often describes projects and conditions.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词已经表示「变好」，动词也就承接了这层比喻义，如今多用来描述工程与状况。

intro.en: Progress comes from a Latin verb that joins forward to walk, and the noun keeps the same image of a journey towards something.
intro.cn: progress 出自一个把「向前」和「走」合起来的拉丁动词，名词里仍保留着「朝某处走」的画面。

items.en: The prefix pro- meant forward, and gradi meant to walk or to step, so the two together described stepping onward.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向前，动词 gradi 表示走、迈步，两者合起来就是「向前迈」。

items.en: Progredi meant to go forward, to advance, and its past participle progressus supplied the noun.
items.cn: progredi 意为前进、推进，其过去分词 progressus 提供了名词形式。

items.en: Progressus named a going forward, both on the ground and in the course of events.
items.cn: progressus 指向前行进，既指脚下的路，也指事情的进程。

items.en: Old French progres kept the noun sense of advance and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 progres 保留「前进」的名词义，并传入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses progress for movement and improvement, and also as a verb; the noun stresses the first syllable and the verb the second.
items.cn: 现代英语用 progress 表示行进与进步，也可作动词；名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin root of stepping; the near-meaning group gathers words for moving and getting better.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「迈步」词根上的词；近义组收表示前行与变好的词。

entries.definition: Moving forward step by step, or favouring social reform.
entries.definitionCN: 一步步向前的；主张社会改革的。

entries.definition: A series of steps or stages in a process.
entries.definitionCN: 过程中的一连串步骤或阶段。

entries.definition: To move backwards to an earlier or worse state.
entries.definitionCN: 退回较早或较差的状态。

entries.definition: Happening slowly, in small steps.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢发生的，一步一步的。

entries.definition: Forward movement, or a step towards a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 向前移动，或朝目标迈出的一步。

entries.definition: The process of growing or becoming more advanced.
entries.definitionCN: 成长或变得更先进的过程。

entries.definition: A change that makes something better.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变好的改变。

entries.definition: Forward movement, especially against difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指克服困难后的前进。

normalIntro.en: The word is a walk turned into a picture of improvement, and its family keeps the same forward step.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把「走路」变成「变好」的比喻，同族词都保留着那一步向前的动作。

normal.en: Latin gradi means to walk, so progress is first a matter of feet, not of grades.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「走」，所以 progress 最初说的是脚步，而不是分数。

normal.en: The prefix pro- points forward, which is why progress always carries a direction.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 指向前方，所以 progress 总带着方向感。

normal.en: The noun puts the beat on the first syllable and the verb on the second, as English often does with such pairs.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节，英语里这类成对的词常常如此。

normal.en: Progressive adds -ive: a person or policy that keeps moving forward.
normal.cn: progressive 加 -ive，指不断向前的人或政策。

normal.en: Progression adds -ion: the series of steps that a forward movement leaves behind.
normal.cn: progression 加 -ion，指前进过程中留下的一连串步骤。

abstract.en: A journey and an improvement share one word because both are measured by where you were and where you are.
abstract.cn: 旅程和进步共用一个词，因为两者都要靠「原来在哪、现在在哪」来衡量。

abstract.en: Progress is invisible in a single moment; it only appears when you look back at the distance covered.
abstract.cn: 进度在单独一刻里看不见，只有回头看走过的距离时才显现。

abstract.en: The same word can be a thing and an action, which is why English can say that progress progresses.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能是事物也能是动作，所以英语里可以说 progress 自己在前行。

examples.en: She has made real progress in her spoken English.
examples.cn: 她的英语口语有了实实在在的进步。

examples.en: The procession progressed slowly along the narrow street.
examples.cn: 队伍沿着窄街缓慢前行。

examples.en: Negotiations are still in progress.
examples.cn: 谈判仍在进行中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若格瑞斯」——听着像「扑过去，格外卖力」，往前一扑再使劲，就是进步。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ gradi（走）构成 progredi，过去分词 progressus 意为「向前走」，经古法语 progres 进入英语；名词重音在前，动词重音在后。

sensesIntro.en: The core is walking forward; the senses split into the journey itself, the improvement it stands for, and the two verb uses that follow.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向前走」；义项分成脚下的行进、由它比喻出的进步，以及随之而来的两种动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group of walkers moving steadily along a ridge, with the ground already covered stretching out behind them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人沿着山脊稳步向前，走过的路在身后越拉越长。

branches.en: a column of walkers rounding a bend
branches.cn: 一队行人绕过弯道

branches.en: a learner reading a page that once looked impossible
branches.cn: 学习者读着一页曾经觉得很难读的文字

branches.en: a river of people moving through a narrow street
branches.cn: 人流沿着窄街向前移动

branches.en: a building site gaining a floor each month
branches.cn: 工地每个月多出一层

branches.en: a project that is visibly further along than last year
branches.cn: 比去年明显推进了的项目

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of walking, with English endings added later.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示向前的拉丁语前缀和表示行走的拉丁语动词构成，英语后缀是后来加上的。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradi, to walk, and its participle progressus sit behind the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradi（走）及其分词 progressus 是英语名词与动词的来源。

definition_zh: 逐步的；渐进的；进步的；主张改革的；（语法）进行体的；（税）累进的；改革派人士
definition_en: moving forward in stages, favouring social reform, or naming a verb form that shows an action still in progress
core_image: 沿着台阶一级一级向上走，每一脚都踩在上一级上
scene: 这套课程的难度会随进度逐步提高。Public health officials described the outbreak as a progressive disease that worsens over months rather than days.
sceneCN: 这里 progressive 是「逐阶段加重的」（第 3 个义项：病情按阶段持续恶化）；句意：公共卫生官员称这次暴发是一种在数月而非数日里逐步加重的疾病。图中可辨识物件：一张张翻过的日历、由浅入深的病情曲线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 渐进的；进步的；主张改革的；进行体的；累进的
改革派人士；（语法）进行体形式

senses.title: Moving ahead in stages
senses.definition: describing change that takes place step by step rather than all at once
senses.definitionCN: 指变化不是一次性完成，而是分阶段一步一步发生的
senses.example: The textbook offers a progressive introduction to statistics, one chapter at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教材一章一节地逐步介绍统计学。
senses.why: Pro- means 'forward' and gradi means 'to step', so progredi was 'to walk forward'. The suffix -ive turns that walk into an adjective for anything that keeps stepping ahead.
senses.whyCN: pro- 意为“向前”，gradi 意为“迈步”，因此 progredi 就是“向前走”。后缀 -ive 把这次行走变成形容词，用来形容任何不断向前迈步的事物。

senses.title: Favouring social reform
senses.definition: supporting changes in law, education or the economy in order to improve society
senses.definitionCN: 支持在法律、教育或经济方面作出改变，以求改善社会
senses.example: The mayor ran on a progressive platform of housing and transit reform.
senses.exampleCN: 这位市长以住房与交通改革的进步纲领参加竞选。
senses.why: Around 1900 the forward-step image was applied to politics: people who wanted society to move ahead began to call themselves progressive.
senses.whyCN: 大约在 1900 年，向前迈步的意象被用到政治上：希望社会向前走的人开始自称 progressive。

senses.title: Growing worse stage by stage
senses.definition: of an illness: continuing to develop and worsen over time in stages
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病随时间分阶段持续发展、逐渐加重
senses.example: Doctors warned that the progressive loss of hearing could not be reversed.
senses.exampleCN: 医生警告说，这种逐步加重的听力丧失无法逆转。
senses.why: Medical usage keeps only the stepping part of the image. The illness keeps advancing step after step, and the direction happens to be bad.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法只保留了意象中“迈步”的部分：疾病一步一步向前推进，只是方向恰好是不好的那一边。

senses.title: Grammar: action still running
senses.definition: the verb form that presents an action as ongoing at a stated moment
senses.definitionCN: 指把动作呈现为在某一时刻仍在持续进行的动词形式
senses.example: English marks ongoing action with the progressive form, as in 'he is reading'.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用进行体标记正在持续的动作，例如“他正在阅读”。
senses.why: The action is pictured mid-stride, caught while it is still walking. Grammarians named the be + -ing form after that unfinished step.
senses.whyCN: 动作被画在半路上，正是在它还在走的时候被抓住。语法学家就用这个未完成的步子来命名 be + -ing 形式。

senses.title: Tax rates that climb with income
senses.definition: of a tax: taking a larger share from higher bands of income
senses.definitionCN: 指对更高收入档次征收更大比例的税
senses.example: Under a progressive income tax, higher earners pay a larger share of their income.
senses.exampleCN: 在累进所得税制下，收入更高的人按其收入缴纳更大比例。
senses.why: Each income band steps up to a higher rate, so the tax ladder rises as the figure rises: the staircase image moved into numbers.
senses.whyCN: 每一收入档次都向上迈到更高的税率，税级随收入上升而上升：台阶的意象被搬进了数字里。

senses.title: Ahead of current thinking
senses.definition: modern in outlook, especially in education, art or social policy
senses.definitionCN: 指在教育、艺术或社会政策上观念现代、走在前面
senses.example: Her progressive views on assessment upset the traditional examiners.
senses.exampleCN: 她在评估方式上的进步观点让传统考官感到不安。
senses.why: Here the forward step measures ideas against the present: whatever stands ahead of current practice is called progressive.
senses.whyCN: 这里向前的一步是用当下衡量观念：凡站在现行做法之前的，就被称为 progressive。

senses.title: A supporter of reform
senses.definition: a person who belongs to or supports a reformist political group
senses.definitionCN: 指属于或支持改革派政治团体的人
senses.example: The committee split between progressives and conservatives over the zoning plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在分区规划上分裂为改革派与保守派。
senses.why: The political adjective was turned into a countable noun in the early 20th century, first in American party language.
senses.whyCN: 这个政治形容词在 20 世纪初被转为可数名词，最早出现在美国政党用语中。

senses.title: The progressive form itself
senses.definition: the grammatical form or construction that expresses ongoing action
senses.definitionCN: 指表达持续动作的语法形式或结构
senses.example: 'Is eating' is a progressive, while 'eats' is a simple present.
senses.exampleCN: “is eating”是进行体，而“eats”是一般现在时。
senses.why: In grammar books the adjective became a countable noun naming the form; the term is short for 'progressive tense' or 'progressive aspect'.
senses.whyCN: 在语法书里，这个形容词变成可数名词来指形式；这个说法是“进行时态”或“进行体”的简称。

intro.en: Progressive joins pro-, 'forward', with gradi, 'to step', and then adds the adjective suffix -ive. The Latin verb progredi meant 'to walk forward', and its participle progressus gave the noun progress. The adjective simply describes whatever keeps stepping ahead, whether a disease, a tax scale, a verb form or a political programme.
intro.cn: progressive 由 pro-“向前”、gradi“迈步”与形容词后缀 -ive 组成。拉丁动词 progredi 意为“向前走”，其分词 progressus 产生了名词 progress。这个形容词只是描述任何不断向前迈步的事物——无论是一种疾病、一张税率表、一个动词形式，还是一套政治纲领。

items.en: The root behind Latin gradi, 'to step', is reconstructed as *ghredh-. It is generally believed to be the source of the Latin words for step and grade.
items.cn: 拉丁 gradi“迈步”背后的词根被重构为 *ghredh-，一般认为它是拉丁语中表示“步、等级”的一组词的来源。

items.en: Gradi was a deponent verb meaning 'to walk, to step'. Its noun partner gradus meant 'a step' and also 'a rank or degree', and both feed the modern word family.
items.cn: gradi 是异态动词，意为“走、迈步”。其名词伙伴 gradus 表示“一步”，也表示“等级、程度”，两者都滋养了现代词族。

items.en: The prefix added direction: progredi meant 'to step forward', and its past participle progressus became the noun for forward movement.
items.cn: 前缀赋予方向：progredi 意为“向前迈步”，其过去分词 progressus 成为表示“前进”的名词。

items.en: French progressif and Medieval Latin progressivus gave English progressive. Early uses were physical: a progressive motion, a progressive disease.
items.cn: 法语 progressif 与中古拉丁 progressivus 给英语带来了 progressive。早期用法是物理性的：向前运动、进行性疾病。

items.en: Reform politics borrowed the forward image: a progressive wanted society to move ahead. Progressive taxation, with rates rising band by band, uses the same staircase in numbers.
items.cn: 改革政治借用了向前的意象：progressive 想让社会向前走。累进税制让税率逐档上升，把同一座台阶搬进了数字里。

items.en: Grammarians named the be + -ing form the progressive because it presents an action caught in the middle of happening, not finished.
items.cn: 语法学家把 be + -ing 形式命名为进行体，因为它呈现的是发生在半途、尚未结束的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun progress, the abstract progression, the adverb and the opposite-prefix regressive. The meaning group contrasts kinds of forward movement and kinds of reform.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词 progress、抽象名词 progression、副词形式与反向前缀的 regressive；词义组比较不同类型的向前推进与不同类型的改革主张。

entries.definition: forward movement or improvement; to move forward. It names the movement itself, while progressive describes something that has that character.
entries.definitionCN: 向前运动或改进；向前推进。它命名运动本身，而 progressive 描述具备这种性质的事物。

entries.definition: a series of steps or stages in order. It stresses sequence, while progressive stresses the direction of travel.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序排列的一系列步骤或阶段。它强调次序，而 progressive 强调行进方向。

entries.definition: in stages, or increasingly. It turns the adjective into a statement about how something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 分阶段地，或越来越……地。它把形容词转为对发生方式的陈述。

entries.definition: moving backward, especially undoing reform. It is built on the same Latin step but with re- 'back' instead of pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 向后退的，尤指取消改革。它建立在同一个拉丁“步”词根上，只是用 re-“向后”取代了 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: far along in development. It says where something stands, not that it moves in stages.
entries.definitionCN: 发展程度高的。它说明某物所处的位置，而不表示它分阶段推进。

entries.definition: happening slowly by small degrees. It shares the step image but carries no political or grammatical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以微小程度缓慢发生的。它共享台阶意象，但不含政治或语法含义。

entries.definition: going on without a break. It stresses an unbroken span, while progressive stresses a series of advancing stages.
entries.definitionCN: 不中断地持续。它强调连续不断，而 progressive 强调一连串前进的阶段。

entries.definition: favouring gradual change in institutions. It is close to senses 02 and 07 but names the doctrine rather than the forward image.
entries.definitionCN: 主张对制度作渐进改革的。它接近第 2 与第 7 义项，但命名的是主张，而非向前的意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word as pro + grad + ive, then let the staircase cover stages, illness, tax bands, grammar and politics.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 pro + grad + ive，再用台阶意象串起阶段、病情、税档、语法与政治。

normal.en: Split it into pro + gress + ive: forward, step, adjective. The word literally means 'stepping forward'.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + gress + ive：向前、迈步、形容词。这个词字面就是“向前迈步的”。

normal.en: Picture a staircase: every step stands on the one below, so nothing jumps to the top.
normal.cn: 想象一座楼梯：每一级都踩在下一级上，没有哪一步能跳到顶端。

normal.en: A progressive disease climbs the same stairs, only downward in terms of health.
normal.cn: 进行性疾病爬的是同一座楼梯，只是在健康上朝下走。

normal.en: In a progressive tax, each income band sits one stair higher than the last.
normal.cn: 在累进税中，每一收入档次都比上一档高一级台阶。

normal.en: A progressive in politics is someone who wants the whole society to take the next step.
normal.cn: 政治上的改革派，就是希望整个社会迈出下一步的人。

abstract.en: Think of time as a ladder rather than a line: 'progressive' always implies rungs, never a smooth slope.
abstract.cn: 把时间想成梯子而不是直线：progressive 总暗示横档，而不是平滑斜坡。

abstract.en: Notice that the medical sense keeps the motion but drops the hope: stepping forward can also mean going further into illness.
abstract.cn: 注意医学义保留了运动却丢掉了希望：向前迈步也可能意味着更深地陷入疾病。

abstract.en: Hold present and progressive apart: one stands still at a point in time, the other is photographed mid-stride.
abstract.cn: 把“现在”与“进行”分开：一个静止在时间点上，另一个被拍在迈步的半途。

examples.en: The school adopted a progressive curriculum that adds one skill level at a time.
examples.cn: 这所学校采用了逐级增加技能的渐进式课程。

examples.en: Specialists tracked the progressive weakening of the patient's muscles.
examples.cn: 专家追踪了病人肌肉逐步变弱的过程。

examples.en: Economists debated whether a progressive tax on vacant land would cool the market.
examples.cn: 经济学家争论对闲置土地征收累进税是否能给市场降温。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗格瑞斯”：一步一扑向前走，越走越进步。

root: 拉丁 progredi“向前走”（pro- 向前 + gradi 迈步），过去分词 progressus，加 -ive 构成形容词；核心意象是“一级一级往前走”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep someone or something walking forward. A course moves through levels, an illness moves through stages, a tax scale moves through bands, a verb form catches an action mid-stride, a reformer wants society to take the next step, and grammar turns the adjective into a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留了“有人在向前走”：课程逐级推进，疾病逐段发展，税率逐档上升，动词形式把动作抓在半途，改革者希望社会迈出下一步，语法则把这个形容词变成名词。

core.en: Stepping forward, one stage at a time, until the new position stands ahead of the old one.
core.cn: 一步一步向前，每迈一步都进入新阶段，直到新的位置站在旧位置之前。

branches.en: STAGES: change arrives one step at a time, whether it improves health or worsens it.
branches.cn: 阶段：变化一步一步到来，无论它让健康变好还是变坏。

branches.en: POLITICS: the forward step becomes a demand for reform and a name for its supporters.
branches.cn: 政治：向前的一步变成改革诉求，也成为支持者的名称。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the action is shown mid-step, and the form itself takes the adjective as a name.
branches.cn: 语法：动作被展示在半步之中，形式本身也借用了这个形容词作名称。

branches.en: NUMBERS: the staircase becomes tax bands that climb with income.
branches.cn: 数字：台阶变成随收入上升的税档。

branches.en: OUTLOOK: ideas are ranked by how far ahead of present practice they stand.
branches.cn: 观念：思想按它们领先当下做法的程度来排序。

intro.en: Progressive stacks pro-, the verb gradi and the adjective suffix -ive. The items below show the same base with other endings, and the opposite prefix re- building the reverse idea.
intro.cn: progressive 叠加了 pro-、动词 gradi 与形容词后缀 -ive。下列条目展示同一词基配其他词尾，以及反向前缀 re- 构成的相反概念。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb, its noun and its participle. They explain why one word family covers walking, ranking, taxation and grammar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词、名词与分词，解释了为什么同一词族能覆盖行走、等级、征税与语法。

items.meaning: moving forward in stages; favouring reform
items.meaningCN: 分阶段向前的；主张改革的
items.example: The reform was introduced in progressive stages.
The report noted steady progress in literacy.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出识字率稳步提高。

items.example: The progression from trainee to supervisor takes years.
items.exampleCN: 从实习生到主管的晋升需要数年。

items.example: The light faded progressively after sunset.
items.exampleCN: 日落之后光线逐渐变暗。

items.meaning: the quality of favouring advance or reform
items.example: Critics questioned the progressiveness of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 批评者质疑该方案的进步性。

items.example: The new fee was criticized as a regressive measure.
items.exampleCN: 这项新收费被批评为倒退措施。

items.example: The paint comes in fine gradations of grey.
items.exampleCN: 这种颜料有细致的灰色层次。
康复虽然缓慢，但很彻底。

latinEntries.meaning: a step; a rank or degree

definition_zh: 禁止；阻止；使不可能；（法律）禁止某人做某事
definition_en: to forbid something by law or rule, or to make it impossible
core_image: 一只手横在门前，掌心朝外，把来人挡回去
scene: 博物馆入口挂着一块牌子。The sign at the entrance says that the rules prohibit flash photography, and the guard raises a hand whenever a camera comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 prohibit 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项：以规则明令不许做某事）；句意：入口的牌子写着规定禁止使用闪光灯，保安一看到有人举相机就抬手示意。图中可辨识物件：禁止标识、相机、闪光灯、保安的手、展厅入口；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 禁止；阻止；使不可能

derivatives.zh: 禁止的；（价格）高得使人却步的

senses.title: Forbid by law or rule
senses.definition: to state officially that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 官方规定某事不得做
senses.example: The law prohibits smoking indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止室内吸烟。
senses.why: Latin prohibere means 'hold back'. The prefix pro- pushes away, and habere holds: the rule puts a hand out and holds the thing back from happening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prohibere 意为“挡住”。前缀 pro- 向外推，habere 是持握：规则伸出一只手，把此事挡在外面。

senses.title: Prevent or make impossible
senses.definition: to make something impossible in practice
senses.definitionCN: 使某事在实践中不可能
senses.example: The high cost prohibits most families from buying.
senses.exampleCN: 高昂的成本使多数家庭无法购买。
senses.why: The same holding-back can be economic rather than legal: price acts like a gate. Prohibitive costs prohibit without any statute.
senses.whyCN: 同一种“挡住”可以是经济的而非法律的：价格像一道门。 prohibitive 的成本无需法规就禁止了购买。

senses.title: Forbid a person from doing
senses.definition: to bar a specific person from an action
senses.definitionCN: 禁止特定的人采取某行动
senses.example: The court prohibited him from contacting her.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭禁止他联系她。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the rule targets an agent rather than an act. The structure prohibit someone from doing marks the boundary drawn around that person.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是人时，规则瞄准行动者而非行为本身。prohibit someone from doing 的结构，标记围绕此人画下的边界。

senses.title: An official ban
senses.definition: to ban something officially, often by authority
senses.definitionCN: 由权威正式取缔某物
senses.example: The city prohibited the sale of fireworks.
senses.exampleCN: 该市禁止销售烟花爆竹。
senses.why: A ban is the institutional form of the hand at the door. Prohibition is the noun, and it can name a whole historical policy, as in the American Prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 禁令是“门口那只手”的制度形式。prohibition 是名词，可以命名一整段历史政策，如美国禁酒令。

senses.title: Of a sign or notice: forbid entry or use
senses.definition: of a sign or instruction, to forbid an action or access
senses.definitionCN: 标识或指示禁止某行为或进入
senses.example: The sign prohibits entry without a badge.
senses.exampleCN: 标牌禁止无证进入。
senses.why: Public space is regulated by visible marks. The verb turns a printed symbol into a rule, and the sign becomes the hand made permanent.
senses.whyCN: 公共空间由可见标记管理。动词把印刷符号变成规则，标牌成了被永久化的那只手。

senses.title: Hinder or prevent (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to hinder or stand in the way of
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：妨碍或挡路
senses.example: Bad weather prohibited our advance.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气阻碍了我们前进。
senses.why: This is the broadest layer: anything that holds you back prohibits you. Modern English narrows the word to rules and practical impossibility.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽的一层：任何挡住你的东西都 prohibit 你。现代英语把这个词收窄到规则与实际不可能。

senses.title: Restrain by legal writ
senses.definition: in law, to restrain an action by authority
senses.definitionCN: 法律中以权威限制某行为
senses.example: The injunction prohibits further construction.
senses.exampleCN: 禁令限制继续施工。
senses.why: Courts issue orders that function as verbal gates. The legal sense specializes the holding-back into a formal instrument with penalties attached.
senses.whyCN: 法院发布命令，功能如同语言的门。法律义把“挡住”专门化为附有惩罚的正式工具。

senses.title: Forbid access
senses.definition: to bar entry to a place
senses.definitionCN: 不许进入某地
senses.example: The area is prohibited to civilians.
senses.exampleCN: 该区域禁止平民进入。
senses.why: Access control is the most physical version: a fence, a guard, a sign. The verb names the rule that the barrier enforces.
senses.whyCN: 出入控制是最物理的版本：围栏、警卫、标牌。动词命名屏障所执行的规则。

intro.en: Prohibit is a holding-back word. Latin prohibere joins pro- 'away' to habere 'hold': to hold something away from you, and therefore to forbid it.
intro.cn: prohibit 是一个“挡住”的词。拉丁语 prohibere 把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合：把某物挡在你之外，因此就是禁止它。

items.en: First recorded as 'forbid, prevent', borrowed from Latin prohibitus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“禁止、阻止”，借自拉丁语 prohibitus。

items.en: prohibitus is the past participle of prohibere 'hold back, keep off, prevent, forbid' = pro- 'away, forth' + habere 'to hold'.
items.cn: prohibitus 是 prohibere 的过去分词，后者意为“挡住、隔开、阻止、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”。

items.en: habere also gives habit, exhibit, inhibit, and ability. The family is about holding, and pro- turns holding into holding away.
items.cn: habere 还生成 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。这个词族关乎持握，而 pro- 把“持握”变成“挡开”。

items.en: The noun prohibition and the adjective prohibitive develop, the latter also taking the sense 'so costly as to prevent'.
items.cn: 名词 prohibition 与形容词 prohibitive 发展出来，后者还取得“贵到使人却步”的义。

items.en: Modern English uses prohibit for legal bans, signs, and practical impossibility, keeping the image of a hand held out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 prohibit 指法律禁令、标识与实际不可能，保留“伸出手挡住”的意象。

note.en: The first group shares the habere root; the second is about verbs that also mean forbidding or preventing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 habere 词根，第二组看同样表示“禁止”或“阻止”的动词。

entries.definition: to restrain or slow down. It uses in- 'in' + habere, holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制；阻碍。它用 in-“在内”+ habere，持握在内。

entries.definition: to show publicly. It is ex- 'out' + habere, holding out.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示。它是 ex-“向外”+ habere，持出在外。

entries.definition: an official ban, or the historical US ban on alcohol.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁令；美国禁酒令。

entries.definition: to order someone not to do something. It is broader and more personal than prohibit.
entries.definitionCN: 命令某人不要做。它比 prohibit 更宽、更对人。

entries.definition: to forbid something officially, often by public authority. It is the plain word behind prohibition.
entries.definitionCN: 官方禁止，常由公共权威发布。它是 prohibition 背后的平实词。

entries.definition: to stop something from happening. It covers both rules and practical obstacles.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事发生。它涵盖规则与实际障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin habere 'hold' with pro- 'away', the inhibit/exhibit family, the sign use, and prohibitive cost.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 habere“持握”加 pro-“向外”、inhibit/exhibit 词族、标识用法，以及 prohibitive cost。

normal.en: Habere means 'hold'; pro- means 'away'. Prohibit is to hold something away from you: a hand at the door.
normal.cn: habere 意为“持握”；pro- 意为“向外”。prohibit 就是把东西挡在你之外：门口的一只手。

normal.en: Inhibit holds in, exhibit holds out, prohibit holds away: the prefix tells you the direction.
normal.cn: inhibit 向内持，exhibit 向外持，prohibit 挡开：前缀告诉你方向。

normal.en: A prohibition sign is the hand made permanent: the rule stays at the door even when no guard is there.
normal.cn: 禁止标识是被永久化的那只手：即使没有警卫，规则仍守在门口。

normal.en: Prohibitive costs prohibit without a law: price acts as a gate.
normal.cn: prohibitive 的成本无需法律就禁止：价格就是门。

normal.en: The word targets both acts and people: you prohibit smoking, and you prohibit someone from smoking.
normal.cn: 这个词既针对行为也针对人：prohibit smoking，也 prohibit someone from smoking。

abstract.en: Every prohibition draws a boundary, and every boundary creates a category of the forbidden.
abstract.cn: 每一项禁令都画出一条边界，每条边界都造出“被禁止者”这一类别。

abstract.en: Forbidding is cheaper than preventing: a rule costs words, a wall costs stone.
abstract.cn: 禁止比阻止便宜：规则花的是话，墙花的是石头。

abstract.en: The same verb covers law and economics, which shows that constraint has many currencies.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖法律与经济，说明约束有多种货币。

examples.en: Smoking is prohibited in all public buildings.
examples.cn: 所有公共建筑内禁止吸烟。

examples.en: The high price prohibits many students from applying.
examples.cn: 高昂的价格使许多学生无法申请。

examples.en: The court prohibited the company from selling the drug.
examples.cn: 法庭禁止该公司销售这种药物。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若黑壁”——扑到黑色的墙壁前被挡住 → prohibit 禁止、阻止

root: 拉丁语 prohibere“挡住、禁止”= pro-“向外”+ habere“持握”；同族有 habit、exhibit、inhibit、ability。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of prohibit, all one gesture: holding something away. The hand can be a law, a sign, a court order, a price, or a fence.
sensesIntro.cn: prohibit 的八个义项，都是同一个手势：把某物挡在外面。这只手可以是法律、标识、法院命令、价格或围栏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out to keep something away.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸出一只手，把某物挡在外面。

branches.en: RULE: laws, bans, and signs state what must not be done.
branches.cn: 规则：法律、禁令与标识规定什么不得做。

branches.en: PERSON AND COURT: an order can be drawn around a specific person or action.
branches.cn: 人与法庭：命令可围绕特定人或行为画界。

branches.en: ACCESS: a barrier enforces the rule at a physical threshold.
branches.cn: 进入：屏障在物理门槛上执行规则。

branches.en: ECONOMICS: price holds people back without any statute.
branches.cn: 经济：价格无需法规就把人挡住。

branches.en: HINDRANCE: the archaic sense covers any obstacle that holds you back.
branches.cn: 妨碍：古义涵盖任何挡住你的障碍。

intro.en: Prohibit is a Latin verb. English adds -ion, -ive, and -ed, and the root habere also builds inhibit, exhibit, and habit.
intro.cn: prohibit 是拉丁动词。英语加 -ion、-ive、-ed，词根 habere 还构成 inhibit、exhibit、habit。

latinIntro.en: Latin prohibere 'hold back' combines pro- 'away' with habere 'hold'. The same habere underlies exhibit (hold out), inhibit (hold in), and habit (what one holds).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prohibere“挡住”把 pro-“向外”与 habere“持握”结合。同一个 habere 支撑 exhibit（持出）、inhibit（持内）与 habit（所持之物）。

definition_zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划；投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）
definition_en: a planned piece of work, or to throw something forward in space, time, or imagination
core_image: 把一张纸向前抛出去，纸面在空中展开成一块可见的平面
scene: 会议室里，团队把目标、时间线、负责人写在墙上。The whole project is pinned to the wall, with its goals, its timeline and the name of the person who owns each part.
sceneCN: 这里 project 是「项目、工程」（第 1 个义项：为达成目标而规划的一整块工作）；句意：整个项目都贴在墙上，写着目标、时间线，以及每一部分的负责人。图中可辨识物件：项目看板、便利贴、时间线、负责人照片、马克笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 项目；工程；课题；计划
投射；凸出；预测；表现（形象）；使（影像）成像

senses.title: A planned piece of work
senses.definition: a planned undertaking with a goal, a timetable, and resources
senses.definitionCN: 有计划、有目标、有时间与资源的任务
senses.example: The bridge project will take five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的工程要五年。
senses.why: Latin proiectum is 'something thrown forward'. A project is a plan thrown ahead of you, a future state you have already sketched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proiectum 是“被抛向前之物”。project 是被投到你前方的计划，一幅你已勾画出的未来图景。

senses.title: A research or study topic
senses.definition: a specific piece of research or academic work
senses.definitionCN: 一项具体的研究或学术工作
senses.example: She is working on a project about urban birds.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做一个关于城市鸟类的课题。
senses.why: Schools and labs cut knowledge into manageable pieces. Each project is a bounded task with its own question, method, and deadline.
senses.whyCN: 学校与实验室把知识切成可处理的块。每个 project 都是有界任务，有自己的问题、方法与期限。

senses.title: To estimate or forecast
senses.definition: to calculate what a quantity will be in the future
senses.definitionCN: 计算某数量在未来会是多少
senses.example: Analysts project a rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计需求上升。
senses.why: Forecasting is throwing a number forward in time. The same verb that launches an object through space launches a figure into next year.
senses.whyCN: 预测是把一个数字抛向未来。同一个把物体抛过空间的动词，也把数字抛进明年。

senses.title: To throw forward physically
senses.definition: to throw or cast something forward
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向前抛
senses.example: The machine projects balls at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器高速抛出球。
senses.why: This is the literal core: iacere 'to throw' with pro- 'forward'. Every abstract sense is a metaphor built on this physical cast.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：iacere“投”加 pro-“向前”。一切抽象义都建在这个物理抛掷上。

senses.title: To cast an image onto a surface
senses.definition: to cause light or an image to fall on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 使光或影像落在某个表面
senses.example: The device projects the map onto the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 设备把地图投射到墙上。
senses.why: Light is thrown forward and lands on a screen. The projector is the object that throws, and the image is what arrives.
senses.whyCN: 光被抛向前方，落在屏幕上。projector 是抛掷之物，影像则是到达之物。

senses.title: To extend outward
senses.definition: of a part, to stick out beyond the main body
senses.definitionCN: 某部分超出主体向外伸
senses.example: The balcony projects over the street.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台向街道上方凸出。
senses.why: A shape that juts out is literally thrown beyond the wall. Architecture uses the word for any part that advances past its base.
senses.whyCN: 向外突出的形状，字面上被抛出了墙外。建筑学用这个词指任何越过基线的部分。

senses.title: To convey an impression
senses.definition: to communicate a quality or image to others
senses.definitionCN: 向他人传达某种品质或形象
senses.example: A good speaker projects confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 好的演讲者展现自信。
senses.why: Social presence is treated as a projection: an inner state is thrown outward so others can see it. The word implies deliberate display.
senses.whyCN: 社会在场被当作一种投射：内在状态被抛到外面，让他人看见。这个词隐含刻意的展示。

senses.title: To predict by extrapolation
senses.definition: to extend a trend or pattern into the future
senses.definitionCN: 把趋势或模式延伸到未来
senses.example: The model projects growth through 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 模型推算增长将持续到 2030 年。
senses.why: Statistics throws a line forward from known points. Projection is the noun, and it always carries the caveat that the future may not land where the line points.
senses.whyCN: 统计把一条线从已知点向前抛。projection 是名词，且总带着警告：未来未必落在线的落点。

senses.title: To protrude anatomically
senses.definition: of a body part, to stick out from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分从表面突出
senses.example: The jaw projects forward.
senses.exampleCN: 下颌向前突出。
senses.why: Bones and features can be thrown beyond the body's outline. Anatomy uses the same spatial verb as architecture, applied to flesh.
senses.whyCN: 骨与特征可以超出身体轮廓。解剖学把与建筑相同的空间动词用于肉体。

senses.title: To map onto a plane (geometry)
senses.definition: to represent a figure on a plane by drawing lines from it
senses.definitionCN: 用射线把图形表示到平面上
senses.example: Project the sphere onto a flat map.
senses.exampleCN: 把球面投影到平面地图上。
senses.why: Geometry formalizes the light image: points are carried along rays to a surface. Map projections keep the same metaphor, with distortion as the price.
senses.whyCN: 几何学把光的意象形式化：点沿射线被带到表面。地图投影保留同一隐喻，代价是变形。

intro.en: Project is a throwing word. Latin proicere joins pro- 'forward' to iacere 'to throw'. A plan, an image, a forecast, and a balcony are all things thrown ahead of the body.
intro.cn: project 是一个抛掷词。拉丁语 proicere 把 pro-“向前”与 iacere“投”结合。计划、影像、预测与阳台，都是被抛到身体前方的东西。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as 'a plan, scheme, design'.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为“计划、方案、设计”。

items.en: From Latin proiectum 'something thrown forth', neuter past participle of proicere 'throw forward' = pro- 'forward' + iacere 'to throw'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 proiectum“被抛向前之物”，是 proicere“向前抛”的中性过去分词 = pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”。

items.en: iacere also gives eject, inject, reject, subject, and object. The family is about throwing, and the prefix sets the direction.
items.cn: iacere 还生成 eject、inject、reject、subject、object。这个词族关乎投掷，前缀定方向。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense 'to throw or cast forward'.
items.cn: 动词出现，义为“向前投掷”。

items.en: Projection extends to optics, psychology (projecting an image), and statistics (projecting a trend).
items.cn: projection 扩展到光学、心理学（投射形象）与统计学（推算趋势）。

items.en: Modern English uses project for both a planned task and the act of throwing an image, a forecast, or a shape forward.
items.cn: 现代英语用 project 既指计划任务，也指把影像、预测或形状向前抛出的动作。

note.en: The first group shares the iacere root and the -ject shape; the second is about words that also mean a plan or a forecast.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iacere 词根与 -ject 形态，第二组看同样表示“计划”或“预测”的词。

entries.definition: to throw back; to refuse. It is re- 'back' + iacere.
