entries.definition: a detailed proposal for doing something. It emphasizes intention, not the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的详细提议。它强调意图，而非工作本身。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It matches project sense 3 but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将发生之事的陈述。它对应 project 第 3 义，但更具体。

entries.definition: a risky new business or activity. It stresses risk rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 有风险的新事业。它强调风险，而非规划。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin iacere 'throw', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the reject/inject/eject family, and the optics and statistics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 iacere“投”、前缀 pro-“向前”、reject/inject/eject 词族，以及光学与统计用法。

normal.en: Iacere means 'throw'; pro- means 'forward'. A project is something thrown ahead of you.
normal.cn: iacere 意为“投”；pro- 意为“向前”。project 是被抛到你前方的东西。

normal.en: Reject throws back, inject throws in, eject throws out, project throws forward: the prefix is the direction.
normal.cn: reject 掷回，inject 掷入，eject 掷出，project 掷向前：前缀就是方向。

normal.en: A projector throws light; a balcony throws itself beyond the wall; a forecast throws a number into next year.
normal.cn: 投影仪抛光；阳台把自己抛出墙外；预测把数字抛进明年。

normal.en: Project management is planning seen as a launched object: it has a target, a trajectory, and a landing date.
normal.cn: 项目管理就是把计划看作被发射的物体：它有目标、弹道与落地日期。

normal.en: Projecting confidence is throwing an inner state outward so others can catch it.
normal.cn: 展现自信，是把内在状态抛到外面，让他人接住。

abstract.en: Planning is projective: to make a project is to live in a future you have already thrown into view.
abstract.cn: 规划是投射性的：做一个项目，就是住在一个已被你抛入视野的未来里。

abstract.en: Every projection distorts: a map, a forecast, and a self-image all flatten something three-dimensional.
abstract.cn: 每一种投影都会变形：地图、预测与自我形象，都把某种立体之物压平。

abstract.en: The word ties action to imagination: what we throw forward is first an object of thought, then a thing in the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词把行动与想象绑在一起：我们抛向前方的，先是思想的对象，然后才是世界中的实物。

examples.en: The team finished the project ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 团队提前完成了项目。

examples.en: The film was projected onto a huge screen.
examples.cn: 影片被投射到一块巨大的屏幕上。

examples.en: Sales are projected to grow by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额预计增长百分之十。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若杰克特”——扑向前，像杰克特（飞镖）一样被抛出 → project 项目、投射

root: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”= pro-“向前”+ iacere“投”；过去分词 proiectum。同族有 eject、inject、reject、subject。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of project, all one throw. What is thrown can be a plan (a project), an image (a projection), a number (a forecast), a wall (a balcony), or a self (a persona).
sensesIntro.cn: project 的十个义项，都是同一次抛掷。被抛出的可以是计划（项目）、影像（投影）、数字（预测）、墙体（阳台），或自我（形象）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something thrown forward from the body into space or time.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从身体被抛向前方，进入空间或时间。

branches.en: PLAN: a future task sketched and thrown ahead.
branches.cn: 计划：被勾画并抛向前方的未来任务。

branches.en: CAST: physical throwing, light onto a surface, and geometric projection.
branches.cn: 投射：物理抛掷、光落表面与几何投影。

branches.en: PROTRUDE: a part thrown beyond the outline, in buildings and bodies.
branches.cn: 凸出：在建筑与身体中超出轮廓的部分。

branches.en: PERSONA: an inner state thrown outward for others to see.
branches.cn: 形象：内在状态被抛向外，供他人看见。

branches.en: FORECAST: a number or trend carried into the future.
branches.cn: 预测：被带到未来的数字或趋势。

intro.en: Project is noun and verb. English adds -ion, -or, and -ed, and the root iacere also builds reject, inject, eject, and subject.
intro.cn: project 既是名词也是动词。英语加 -ion、-or、-ed，词根 iacere 还构成 reject、inject、eject、subject。

latinIntro.en: Latin proicere 'throw forward' and its participle proiectum stand beside iacere 'throw'. The -ject family is a set of directions: re- back, in- in, e- out, pro- forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proicere“向前抛”及其分词 proiectum 旁边是 iacere“投”。-ject 词族是一组方向：re- 向后、in- 向内、e- 向外、pro- 向前。

items.meaning: the act of projecting; a forecast; a protruding part
items.meaningCN: 投射；预测；凸出（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: a device that throws an image
estimated for the future; cast forward
to throw under; a topic or a person under rule
to throw against; a thing or an aim

definition_zh: 延长；拉长；使持续更久
definition_en: to make something last longer in time, or to stretch it out in length
core_image: 两只手抓住一根绳子，往两头慢慢拉，绳子变得更长
scene: 会谈已经拖到深夜，桌上的人都看着钟，谁也不愿先起身。The chairman refused to prolong the discussion and closed the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里取「延长、使持续更久」的意思（第 1 个义项：让某件事持续更久）；句意为主席不愿再把讨论拖长，于是宣布散会。

pos.zh: 延长；拉长；使（时间）持续更久

derivatives.zh: 由 prolong 加 -ation 构成，义为「延长；延期」
由 prolong 的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「持续很久的；长时间的」

senses.title: To make something last longer
senses.definition: to make an event, a state or a period continue for a longer time
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件、状态或时期持续更久
senses.example: Nothing could prolong the summer beyond September.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能让夏天延续到九月之后。
senses.why: Latin longus means long, and the prefix pro- pushes outward, so the word starts from stretching something out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 longus 意为「长」，前缀 pro- 表示向外推，所以这个词的起点是「把东西往外拉长」。

senses.title: To make a hard experience drag on
senses.definition: to keep an unpleasant situation or feeling going when it could end
senses.definitionCN: 在本可结束时让不愉快的处境或感受继续下去
senses.example: Refusing to decide only prolonged the uncertainty for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 迟迟不做决定，只是让所有人的不确定感拖得更久。
senses.why: If length can be added to anything, it can be added to pain, so the word often carries the sense of needlessly extending what people want to end.
senses.whyCN: 既然长度可以加在任何东西上，也能加在痛苦上，于是这个词常带「把人们盼着结束的事无谓地拖长」的意味。

senses.title: To stretch something out in length
senses.definition: to extend something in physical length, a formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 从物理长度上把某物拉长，属正式或文学用法
senses.example: The low sun prolonged every shadow across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 低垂的太阳把田野上每道影子都拉得很长。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply long, and when the object is a shadow or a line the word returns to that plain idea of length.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「长」，当宾语是影子或线条时，这个词又回到最朴素的长度概念。

intro.en: Prolong joins a Latin prefix of outward movement to the Latin word for long, and French carried the verb into English.
intro.cn: prolong 把表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀接在表示「长」的拉丁词上，再由法语把动词带进英语。

items.en: The prefix pro- meant forward or outward, and longus meant long, so the pair pictured something drawn out at length.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向前、向外，形容词 longus 表示长，两者合起来就是「往外拉长」。

items.en: Prolongare meant to lengthen, to draw out, and it was used of both time and physical extent.
items.cn: prolongare 意为加长、拉长，时间和空间长度都能用它。

items.en: Old French prolonger kept the verb's sense of making something last or reach further.
items.cn: 古法语 prolonger 保留了「使某物更持久、伸得更远」的意思。

items.en: Middle English took the verb and used it mostly in the sense of adding time to something.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个动词，多指给某事加上时间。

items.en: Modern English uses prolong mainly for time, and keeps the physical sense in literary descriptions of light, shadows and lines.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prolong 主要用于时间，物理意义上的拉长则多见于对光、影与线条的文学描写。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for long; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for adding extent or time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「长」形容词上的词；近义组收表示加长长度或时间的动词。

entries.definition: To make something longer, especially in shape.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变长，尤指形状上的拉长。

entries.definition: Long life, or the length of a life.
entries.definitionCN: 长寿；寿命的长短。

entries.definition: The distance east or west measured in degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 以度数计量的东西方向距离；经度。

entries.definition: To make something longer or larger in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上使某物更长或更大。

entries.definition: To become or make longer.
entries.definitionCN: 变长；使变长。

entries.definition: To pull something so that it covers more space.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拉展到占更多空间。

entries.definition: To make something take longer than necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事拖得比必要的时间更长。

normalIntro.en: The word is a rope being pulled longer, and its family keeps returning to length and to time added on.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一根被拉长的绳子，同族词反复回到「长度」和「被加上去的时间」。

normal.en: Latin longus also gives English longitude, so the idea of length sits inside prolong from the start.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 longus 还给英语带来 longitude，所以「长度」这个观念从一开始就在 prolong 里面。

normal.en: The prefix pro- pushes outward, so the rope leaves the hand rather than staying still.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向外推，所以绳子是离开手心、被拉出去的。

normal.en: Prolongation adds -ation to the verb: the act of making something longer.
normal.cn: prolongation 在动词后加 -ation，指「使某物变长」这件事。

normal.en: We prolong life, meetings and agony, but the word often leans towards what people already wish would end.
normal.cn: 我们说延长寿命、延长会议、延长痛苦，而这个词常偏向人们本来就盼着结束的事。

normal.en: The adjective prolonged comes straight from the past participle and describes anything that has been drawn out.
normal.cn: 形容词 prolonged 直接来自过去分词，描述任何被拉长了的事物。

abstract.en: Anything measured in time can be stretched, which is why a word for length ends up meaning delay.
abstract.cn: 凡是用时间衡量的东西都能被拉长，所以一个表示长度的词最后也指拖延。

abstract.en: Prolonging is rarely neutral: adding time to something people want to end is adding weight to it.
abstract.cn: 延长很少是中性的：给人们盼着结束的事加上时间，等于给它加上重量。

abstract.en: A shadow and a meeting can share one verb because both are lines that someone draws out.
abstract.cn: 影子和会议能共用一个动词，因为两者都是被谁拉长的一根线。

examples.en: Regular exercise can prolong your life.
examples.cn: 经常锻炼可以延长寿命。

examples.en: They prolonged the meeting by arguing over details.
examples.cn: 他们为细节争论，把会议拖长了。

examples.en: A prolonged drought has dried up the river.
examples.cn: 长久干旱使这条河干涸了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若龙」——往前一扑像条长龙，越拉越长，就是延长。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、向外）+ longus（长）构成 prolongare，本义「往外拉长」，经古法语 prolonger 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is stretching something outward; the senses divide into added time, needlessly added suffering, and the older physical stretching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西往外拉长」；义项分成加上的时间、无谓拖长的痛苦，以及更古老的物理拉长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pulling a rope apart so that it grows longer and longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手抓住一根绳子往两头拉，绳子越拉越长。

branches.en: a meeting that nobody wants to end
branches.cn: 谁都不愿意散的会议

branches.en: a waiting room where the clock barely moves
branches.cn: 钟几乎不走的候诊室

branches.en: shadows stretching across a field at sunset
branches.cn: 日落时横过田野的长影

branches.en: a low sun drawing a long line of shadow
branches.cn: 低垂的太阳拖出一道长长的影子

branches.en: a decision put off until the worry grows
branches.cn: 被一再推迟、让焦虑加长的决定

intro.en: A Latin prefix of outward movement and the Latin adjective for long hold the word together; French supplied the verb form that English borrowed.
intro.cn: 表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀和表示「长」的拉丁语形容词共同支撑这个词，英语借入的动词形式来自法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin longus, long, and the verb prolongare, to lengthen, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 longus（长）与动词 prolongare（加长）是英语这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 突出的；显眼的；著名的；显要的；重要的；（特征）显著的；（结构）外凸的
definition_en: standing out from a surface or from other people, and therefore easy to notice or important
core_image: 一块石头从墙面上凸出来，走过的人都先看见它
scene: 她的名字出现在海报最显眼的位置。A prominent sandstone arch frames the entrance to the old library.
sceneCN: 这里 prominent 是「向外突出的」（第 3 个义项：结构从墙面伸出、形成门框）；句意：一道突出的砂岩拱券框住了老图书馆的入口。图中可辨识物件：从墙面伸出的拱券、被框住的入口；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 突出的；显眼的；著名的；显要的；显著的

senses.title: Well known and respected
senses.definition: widely known and respected in a particular field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域广为人知并受敬重
senses.example: A prominent economist warned that the housing boom would end.
senses.exampleCN: 一位著名经济学家警告说房地产繁荣将会结束。
senses.why: Prominens meant 'standing out'. Fame is social standing out: the person rises visibly above the ordinary level of the profession.
senses.whyCN: prominens 意为“突出的”。名声就是社会意义上的突出：这个人明显高出于行业的一般水平。

senses.title: Holding an important position
senses.definition: having an important or influential position in an organization or society
senses.definitionCN: 在组织或社会中居于重要或有影响力的位置
senses.example: Several prominent families opposed the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 几个显赫家族反对这项新税。
senses.why: The word moves from visibility to power: a prominent family is one whose name stands out in public affairs and can therefore sway them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从可见度转到权力：显赫家族的名字在公共事务中突出，因此能左右事务。

senses.title: Sticking out from a surface
senses.definition: rising or projecting above the surrounding surface
senses.definitionCN: 高出或伸出周围表面的
senses.example: The old house had prominent stone arches over every window.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子每扇窗上都有突出的石拱。
senses.why: This is the literal core: the thing itself pushes forward beyond the plane it belongs to, so it catches the eye before anything else.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：事物本身顶出所属平面之外，所以比其他东西更早抓住视线。

senses.title: Impossible to overlook
senses.titleCN: 一眼就能看到、难以忽略
senses.definition: placed or shaped so that it is noticed immediately
senses.definitionCN: 放置或造型使其立刻被注意到
senses.example: The safety instructions were printed in a prominent band of red.
senses.exampleCN: 安全说明被印在一条醒目的红色带子上。
senses.why: When designers call a label prominent, they mean it wins the competition for attention against everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 当设计师说某个标签 prominent，意思是它在与周围一切争夺注意力时胜出。

senses.title: Clearly visible in a feature
senses.definition: clearly marked or easily observed, as of a sign or symptom
senses.definitionCN: 指迹象或症状明显、易于观察
senses.example: The first prominent symptom was a persistent dry cough.
senses.exampleCN: 最先出现的明显症状是持续干咳。
senses.why: In medicine the word marks what a clinician cannot miss: a sign that presents itself plainly rather than hiding in the background.
senses.whyCN: 在医学中，这个词标记临床医生不会漏掉的东西：一个直接呈现、不藏在背景里的征象。

senses.title: The leading element
senses.definition: the most important or noticeable element among several
senses.definitionCN: 若干要素中最重要或最引人注意的一个
senses.example: Loss of trust is the most prominent theme in the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 失去信任是这些访谈中最突出的主题。
senses.why: Among competing elements, the prominent one is the one that stands above the rest of the set, much as a bump stands above a surface.
senses.whyCN: 在相互竞争的要素中，突出的那一个是高出其余部分的，就像凸起高出表面。

senses.title: Socially conspicuous
senses.definition: attracting public notice because of wealth, rank or family name
senses.definitionCN: 因财富、地位或家族名望而引人注目
senses.example: The wedding was attended by the town's most prominent citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上最显要的市民都出席了这场婚礼。
senses.why: The social sense specializes in public notice: not merely famous for work, but visible because of rank or wealth.
senses.whyCN: 社会义专门指向公众注意：不仅因工作而出名，更因地位或财富而显眼。

senses.title: Standing out to the eye or ear
senses.definition: visually or acoustically strong enough to dominate the surrounding pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉或听觉上足够强，压过周围的图案或声音
senses.example: A prominent blue stripe runs through the whole fabric.
senses.exampleCN: 一道醒目的蓝色条纹贯穿整块布料。
senses.why: Design and music use the word for the element that dominates the pattern, whether a colour or a beat.
senses.whyCN: 设计与音乐用这个词指压过整体图案的元素，无论是一种颜色还是一个节拍。

intro.en: Prominent is the present participle of Latin prominere, 'to stand out, to project'. Pro- gives the forward push and minere gives the jutting. English borrowed it in the 17th century and let it spread from rocks and bones to reputations, symptoms and design.
intro.cn: prominent 是拉丁 prominere“突出、外伸”的现在分词。pro- 提供向前的推力，minere 提供“伸出”。英语在 17 世纪借入，并让它从岩石与骨骼扩展到名声、症状与设计。

items.en: Minere meant 'to jut or overhang'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; connections with eminere and imminere are generally accepted, while a link to mons 'mountain' remains unproved.
items.cn: minere 意为“伸出、悬突”，更深来源不确定；与 eminere、imminere 的关联一般被接受，而与 mons“山”的联系尚未证实。

items.en: Prominere combined pro- 'forward' with minere 'jut' and meant 'to stand out, to project'. Its participle prominens described whatever was doing the standing out.
items.cn: prominere 由 pro-“向前”与 minere“伸出”组成，意为“突出、外伸”。其分词 prominens 描述正在突出的东西。

items.en: The participle was already used for projecting parts of buildings and bodies, so the adjective carried a physical meaning from the start.
items.cn: 这个分词已用于建筑与身体的外凸部位，因此形容词从一开始就带有物理含义。

items.en: English adopted prominent for physical projections first, then extended it to anything that stood above its surroundings in importance.
items.cn: 英语先借 prominent 指物理凸起，再扩展到任何在重要性上高出周围环境的事物。

items.en: Newspapers made 'prominent citizens' a familiar phrase, and the adjective became the standard word for public standing.
items.cn: 报纸使“显要市民”成为常见说法，这个形容词也成为表示公共地位的标准词。

items.en: Clinical writing adopted prominent for signs that stand out, while design and music used it for elements that dominate a pattern.
items.cn: 临床写作采用 prominent 指明显的征象，设计与音乐则用它指压过整体图案的元素。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from its noun, adverb and the eminence family. The meaning group contrasts being famous, being obvious and being physically raised.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与它的名词、副词形式及 eminence 词族；词义组比较“有名”“明显”与“物理凸起”。

entries.definition: the quality of standing out, or the raised part itself. It names what prominent describes.
entries.definitionCN: 突出的性质，或凸起本身。它命名 prominent 所描述的东西。

entries.definition: in a way that is easy to notice. It tells how something is placed or shown.
entries.definitionCN: 以容易注意的方式。它说明某物如何被放置或展示。

entries.definition: high rank or a height. It comes from eminere, the same jutting verb with e- 'out' instead of pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 高位或高地。它来自 eminere，同一个“伸出”动词，只是用 e-“向外”取代 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: lasting forever. It looks similar but comes from per- 'through' plus manere 'to remain', a completely different root.
entries.definitionCN: 永久的。它看起来相似，却来自 per-“贯穿”加 manere“停留”，词根完全不同。

entries.definition: distinguished and highly respected. It is close to sense 01 but sounds more formal and more about rank.
entries.definitionCN: 卓越且深受敬重的。它接近第 1 义项，但更正式、更强调等级。

entries.definition: clearly visible, often because of unusual appearance. It stresses being seen, while prominent stresses standing above a level.
entries.definitionCN: 明显可见的，常因外形不寻常。它强调被看见，而 prominent 强调高出某一水平。

entries.definition: easy to see or feel. It is the plain everyday word for sense 04.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看到或感觉到的。它是第 4 义项的日常说法。

entries.definition: sticking out physically. It is the narrow word for sense 03, with no fame or importance attached.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上伸出的。它是第 3 义项的窄义说法，不附带名声或重要性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks pin the word to one raised shape, then let it travel from walls to faces, from symptoms to fame.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词钉在一个隆起的形状上，再让它从墙面走到面孔、从症状走到名声。

normal.en: Split it as pro + min + ent: forward + jut + adjective. Anything that juts forward is prominent.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + min + ent：向前、伸出、形容词。凡是向前伸出的就是 prominent。

normal.en: Picture a wall with one brick pushed out: your hand finds that brick first.
normal.cn: 想象一面墙里有一块砖被顶了出来：你的手最先摸到那块砖。

normal.en: Prominent teeth and a prominent nose are the same brick, moved to a face.
normal.cn: 突出的牙齿与高鼻梁就是同一块砖，被移到了脸上。

normal.en: A prominent symptom is the brick in a medical chart: the one the doctor circles.
normal.cn: 明显症状就是病历里的那块砖：医生会把它圈出来。

normal.en: A prominent scientist is the same brick in a crowd: the one the reporters call first.
normal.cn: 著名科学家就是人群里的那块砖：记者最先打电话给他。

abstract.en: The word always needs a background: a bump on a bump is not prominent, only a bump on a flat surface is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终需要背景：凸起上的凸起并不突出，只有平面上的凸起才突出。

abstract.en: Keep fame and shape in one frame: the person stands out socially exactly as the brick stands out physically.
abstract.cn: 把名声与形状放在同一个框架里：人在社会上突出，正如砖头在物理上突出。

abstract.en: Watch the suffix: prominent describes, prominence names, prominently tells how.
abstract.cn: 留意后缀：prominent 描述，prominence 命名，prominently 说明方式。

examples.en: A prominent legal scholar argued that the ruling was too broad.
examples.cn: 一位著名法学学者主张该判决范围过宽。

examples.en: The bird's most prominent feature is the bright red crest on its head.
examples.cn: 这种鸟最显著的特征是头顶鲜红的冠羽。

examples.en: Warning signs were mounted in prominent positions along the cliff path.
examples.cn: 警示牌被安装在悬崖步道的显眼位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗米能特”：一块米能特别突出，从平面上顶出来。

root: 拉丁 prominere 的现在分词 prominens“突出的”（pro- 向前 + minere 伸出）；核心是“从平面顶出来、一眼看见”。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one thing standing above another: a scholar above peers, a family above society, a stone above a wall, a label above text, a symptom above silence, a theme above its rivals, a citizen above the town, a stripe above the fabric.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一物高出另一物：学者高出同行，家族高出社会，石头高出墙面，标签压过文字，症状压过沉默，主题压过其他主题，市民高出小镇，条纹压过布料。

core.en: A part that rises above its background, so that attention lands on it before anything else.
core.cn: 一部分高出背景，因此注意力先落在它上面。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a person rises above peers by reputation or position.
branches.cn: 人：一个人凭名声或地位高出同侪。

branches.en: SHAPE: a part pushes out of its surface and dominates the pattern.
branches.cn: 形状：一部分顶出表面，压过整体图案。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: what stands out is noticed at once, in a room or on a chart.
branches.cn: 可见度：突出的东西立刻被注意到，无论在房间里还是在图表上。

branches.en: COMPETITION: among rival elements, one stands above the rest of the set.
branches.cn: 竞争：在相互竞争的要素中，有一个高出其余。

branches.en: SOCIETY: rank and wealth make a family visible in public life.
branches.cn: 社会：地位与财富让一个家族在公共生活中显眼。

intro.en: Prominent is a Latin participle used as an adjective. The items below show the same jutting verb through noun, adverb and the sibling prefixes e- and in-.
intro.cn: prominent 是拉丁分词用作形容词。下列条目沿着同一个“伸出”动词，走过名词、副词与同胞前缀 e-、in-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its participle. They explain why prominent, prominence and eminence keep the same core image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词与分词，解释为什么 prominent、prominence 与 eminence 保持同一个核心意象。

items.example: A prominent ridge hides the valley from view.
items.exampleCN: 一道突出的山脊挡住了山谷的视线。

items.meaning: the state of standing out; a bump
items.example: The tower's prominence makes it a landmark.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔的突出使它成为地标。

items.example: The flag was prominently hung above the door.
items.exampleCN: 旗帜显眼地挂在门上方。

items.example: The hill's eminence gives a view of the bay.
items.exampleCN: 这座山丘的高起让人能看到海湾。

items.example: An eminent critic praised the first novel.
items.exampleCN: 一位著名评论家称赞了这部处女作。
